answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by completing repeated escrowed trades with distinct counterparties who also have established histories; each trade locks a bond that is forfeited if either party is later proven to have colluded or defaulted. A falcon operator cannot cheaply multiply identities, because every new account needs separate capital and real partners, while coordinated trades expose links through shared funding and timing. The inlet records those links, and a prism of independent audits raises the chance that a fabricated network is caught.
